subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma: staging, resectability criteria, systemic chemotherapy and germline BRCA management

steps.tx: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma staging relies strictly upon high-resolution triphasic helical pancreatic CT to define vascular involvement and categorize tumours as **resectable**, borderline resectable, locally advanced unresectable, or metastatic. Resectable disease requires clear fat planes around the **celiac axis**, superior mesenteric artery, and common hepatic artery, without venous abutment or occlusion of the superior mesenteric and portal veins.
steps.say: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma staging relies strictly upon high-resolution triphasic helical pancreatic CT to define vascular involvement and categorize tumours as resectable, borderline resectable, locally advanced unresectable, or metastatic. Resectable disease requires clear fat planes around the celiac axis, superior mesenteric artery, and common hepatic artery, without venous abutment or occlusion of the superior mesenteric and portal veins.

rows: No contact, or < 180 degrees without vein contour irregularity

steps.tx: The scan shows a pancreatic head tumour wrapping more than half the circumference of the superior mesenteric artery and celiac trunk with contact on the portal vein. This pattern defines **locally advanced disease** rather than a **resectable tumour** because arterial encasement removes clear fat planes used for staging. Such **vascular involvement** places the cancer beyond upfront surgery and favors systemic therapy first. Study the vessel contact to assign resectability correctly.
steps.say: This image shows a pancreatic head cancer encasing the superior mesenteric artery and celiac trunk with contact on the portal vein. Encasement beyond half the vessel circumference marks locally advanced unresectable disease on staging CT. Clear fat planes around these arteries plus a patent vein define resectable cancer instead. Recognizing this degree of vessel contact matters because it directs patients away from upfront surgery toward systemic therapy. Use the vessel relationship to place each tumour in the correct resectability category.

steps.tx: In patients undergoing complete macroscopically clear R0 or R1 resection, the landmark **PRODIGE 24/CCTG PA.6** randomized trial established **adjuvant modified FOLFIRINOX** for 6 months as the global standard of care. Delivering oxaliplatin, irinotecan, and infusional fluorouracil achieved a remarkable median overall survival of 54 months compared to 35 months with gemcitabine monotherapy.

right.title: Gemcitabine Monotherapy
points: Reserved for patients with borderline performance status

steps.tx: In advanced metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma, first-line evidence-based systemic therapy comprises modified FOLFIRINOX or gemcitabine combined with **nab-paclitaxel**. In the pivotal **MPACT trial**, adding nanoparticle albumin-bound paclitaxel to gemcitabine significantly improved overall survival, progression-free survival, and objective response rates over gemcitabine monotherapy, providing an essential first-line option for patients ineligible for intensive triplet regimens.

In the pivotal MPACT trial, adding nanoparticle albumin-bound paclitaxel to gemcitabine significantly improved overall survival, progression-free survival, and objective response rates over gemcitabine monotherapy, providing an essential first-line option for patients ineligible for intensive triplet regimens.

rows: Younger fit patients, ECOG 0-1, normal bilirubin
Acceptable in ECOG 0-2 and mild hyperbilirubinaemia
Palliative frail patients, ECOG 2 or higher

steps.tx: The randomized phase III **NAPOLI 3** trial evaluated first-line **NALIRIFOX**, combining liposomal irinotecan with 5-fluorouracil, leucovorin, and oxaliplatin in metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. NALIRIFOX demonstrated statistically significant improvements in both overall survival and progression-free survival over gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel, confirming liposomal irinotecan-based triplet chemotherapy as a premier front-line option for fit individuals.

steps.tx: In patients with metastatic pancreatic cancer harbouring pathogenic **germline BRCA1** or BRCA2 variants without progression on first-line platinum-based chemotherapy, the phase III **POLO trial** established maintenance therapy with the PARP inhibitor **olaparib**. Maintenance olaparib significantly doubled progression-free survival from 3.8 to 7.4 months compared to placebo, confirming synthetic lethality in homologous recombination repair-deficient pancreatic adenocarcinoma.

right.title: Placebo Maintenance
points: Rapid disease progression off active therapy

steps.tx: Activating **KRAS point mutations** represent the hallmark initiating genetic event occurring in over 90% of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinomas. The vast majority of alterations involve codon 12, predominantly **G12D**, G12V, and G12R substitutions, which lock the GTPase in an active GTP-bound conformation and drive downstream proliferative signalling through RAF-MEK-ERK and PI3K-Akt cascades.

rows: Novel pan-KRAS and GTPase switch-pocket inhibitors
Distinctive biochemical properties; emerging small molecules
Sotorasib and adagrasib approved for G12C-mutant subset

steps.tx: For localized tumours situated in the head or uncinate process of the pancreas, surgical **Pancreaticoduodenectomy** Whipple procedure provides the only potentially curative therapy. The procedure requires en bloc resection of the pancreatic head, duodenum, proximal jejunum, gallbladder, distal bile duct, and partial gastrectomy, demanding microscopically clear **resection margins** R0 to achieve long-term survival.

steps.tx: Baseline serum **CA 19-9** provides essential clinical staging value in localized pancreatic adenocarcinoma. An elevated serum CA 19-9 concentration above 1000 U/mL in patients presenting with anatomically resectable primary tumours strongly correlates with occult peritoneal or distant **micrometastatic disease**, warranting staging diagnostic laparoscopy prior to planned curative laparotomy.
